function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is any vpn is installed". They want to know if any VPN is installed on the system. We need to check if any VPN software is installed. We can use the tool cmd_controller_execute to run a command. On Windows, we can query installed programs via WMIC or PowerShell. Let's try WMIC product get name. That will list installed products. Then we can parse output. But we can't parse here; we just return the command execution result. We'll call the tool with command "wmic product get name" and maybe pipe to findstr for known VPN names like "OpenVPN", "Cisco AnyConnect", "NordVPN", "ExpressVPN", "TunnelBear", "ProtonVPN", "Surfshark", "CyberGhost", "Private Internet Access", "Hotspot Shield", "VyprVPN", "IPVanish", "StrongVPN", "Windscribe", "PPTP", "L2TP", "IKEv2", "WireGuard". But we can't parse. We can just run wmic product get name. That might produce a long list. But we can also filter with findstr. Let's do "wmic product get name | findstr /i \"vpn\"". That will show lines containing vpn. But some names may not contain vpn. Let's include common ones: "OpenVPN", "Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client", "Cisco Secure Client", "Cisco Secure Endpoint", "Cisco Secure VPN", "Cisco AnyConnect", "Cisco Secure Desktop", "Cisco Secure Mobile Client", "Cisco Secure VPN Client", "Cisco Secure Endpoint", "Cisco Secure Endpoint", "Cisco Secure Endpoint", "Cisco Secure Endpoint". But we can just search for "vpn" and "openvpn" etc. Let's do "wmic product get name | findstr /i \"vpn openvpn\"". That will match lines containing vpn or openvpn. But findstr supports multiple patterns separated by space. So "findstr /i \"vpn openvpn\"" will match lines containing either vpn or openvpn. That should catch many. Let's do that.

We'll call the tool with command: "wmic product get name | findstr /i \"vpn openvpn\"". That will list installed products containing vpn or openvpn. We'll then see output. If nothing returned, no VPN installed. If something returned, we can mention those names. We'll just return the output.
